concept.title: Math and Equations
concept.abstract: This section covers Mathematical Equations — quantitative expressions that cannot be represented accurately through prose alone — and five scenarios: a block equation, an inline equation, an equation in a table cell, an equation in a list item, and an equation in a procedure step. The converter maps Word's native OMML equations to <foreign> containing embedded MathML; MathType objects and image-based equations map to <image> with a required <alt> element carrying the equation's accessible text description.

conbody.p: Mathematical equations communicate quantitative relationships that cannot be expressed accurately through prose alone. They are commonly used in engineering, scientific, financial, and technical documentation to represent formulas, calculations, algorithms, and symbolic expressions, and physical constants appear across engineering, scientific, financial, and technical documentation.
The mathematical equation can be inserted as:

ul.li: Word Equation Editor (OMML) -Word's built-in equation editor stores expressions as Office Math Markup Language — a structured, machine-readable XML vocabulary embedded directly in the document body. This is the only mechanism that produces structured MathML in the DITA output.
MathType objects - MathType is a third-party equation editor that embeds equations as OLE (Object Linking and Embedding) binary objects
Image-based equations - An equation represented as a PNG, EMF, or other image file — whether inserted directly or produced by a screenshot — carries no mathematical structure.
Reference-based equations – An equation is stored separately as an external MathML file, which can be reused or maintained outside the topic.
